newsitem.title: UK: UK SFO not to investigate NatWest Markets loss.
newsitem.headline: UK SFO not to investigate NatWest Markets loss.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) which investigates cases of serious or complex fraud, said on Wednesday it will not be launching a criminal investigation into losses incurred by NatWest Markets in interest rate options.

Earlier this year, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank lost 90 million pounds ($151 million)in the interest rate options market. The losses led to the resignation of its chief executive and other senior staff. The SFO said the public interest would best be served by the case being dealt with by the financial market regulator.

"The SFO has carefully considered the circumstances surrounding the losses incurred by NWM in the interest rate options business and has decided that an investigation with a view to a criminal prosecution is not justified," the SFO statement said.

It added that SFO director Rosalind Wright had taken into account the nature of the transactions involved, which were highly complex, and the powers of the regulatory authorities in this area. "She (Wright) takes the view that the public interest in...this case would be more appropriately satisfied by the matter being dealt with by regulation," the statement added.

The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), which regulates market trading and can discipline companies as well as individuals, said it was continuing to study a report into the affair and is reviewing the role of a number of individuals.

An SFA spokesman said the regulator would "undoubtedly have to gather additional information" and could not comment on when this process would be completed. NatWest Markets said it accepted the SFO's decision and had co-operated fully. ($ = 0.594 British Pounds)
